items.body_md:
On August 8, Skillz Platform Inc. filed three deposition notices — targeting Oriel Bachar (Dkt. 54), Pinni Yaniv (Dkt. 55), and James Kong (Dkt. 53) — in connection with its opposition to the Chapter 15 recognition petition, accompanied by a notice of service (Dkt. 52). These are discovery logistics ancillary to the recognition contest; they carry no independent bearing on recovery or timing. The two Latham & Watkins pro hac vice motions filed August 7 (Dkts. 50–51, Michael Ardeljan and Amy Quartarolo) are similarly administrative. No new filings have appeared since, and no press coverage beyond the __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__ report of August 9 — itself covered in the prior edition — has emerged.

The deposition targets are nonetheless worth noting as a structural signal, not a new development. Bachar is the petitioner and Papaya's CEO; Yaniv and Kong are not publicly identified in the docket descriptions, but Skillz's election to notice all three witnesses before the recognition hearing indicates it intends to contest the factual predicate of the petition — most likely the center-of-main-interests determination — rather than rest on legal argument alone. Whether that effort gains traction turns on what Judge Walrath finds credible about the nature and location of Papaya's insolvency proceedings, a question the recognition hearing is designed to resolve. The structural gap between the approximately $719 million disgorgement award plus approximately $10.1 million in fees and costs ordered by Judge Cote, per __[Calcalist / CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/idop8ipjs)__, and the approximately $100 million fund expected to be held in Tel Aviv during 2026, per __[World Casino Directory](https://news.worldcasinodirectory.com/papaya-gaming-files-chapter-15-after-719m-verdict-123873)__, remains unchanged.

The next hard milestones are the objection deadline of August 27, 2026, and the recognition hearing before Judge Walrath on September 3, 2026 at 9:30 AM (virtual).

items.body_md:
On August 7, an objection was docketed at Dkt. 98 — filed on the objection deadline for the bidding-procedures and sale motion — with an accompanying document at Dkt. 99 and an exhibit at Dkt. 100, filed August 8. The filer and substantive content of Dkt. 98 are not established from available docket text, and the relationship of Dkt. 100 to the objection — whether it responds to, supplements, or is independent of it — is unconfirmed. What is confirmed is that Judge O'Hagan will arrive at Thursday's August 14 hearing with at least one live objection on record. The Meeting of Creditors entry at Dkt. 97 is administrative and does not bear on the recovery analysis. The Notice of Docketing Error, carrying no assigned number, is similarly immaterial.

Thor CALAP LLC's no-cause diligence termination right under both purchase agreements expired August 9. No termination notice has appeared on the docket, and no press report has confirmed either an exercise or a waiver. That absence is consistent with both agreements remaining operative but is not confirmatory: Thor may deliver a termination notice directly to the debtors without an immediate court filing. 
The two purchase agreements — covering the Pyote and Tarbush sites in a combined $52 million proposed transaction — gave Thor the right to terminate either deal over unsatisfactory diligence through August 9, five days before the court's scheduled bidding-procedures hearing.
 What confirmation looks like remains unchanged: a debtors' statement that the agreements are in effect, a termination notice on the docket, or a procedural posture at Thursday's hearing that proceeds on the assumption the stalking-horse is intact. None of those has surfaced. The status of the $52 million floor is unverified.


The Assumed Contracts and Excluded Assets schedules remain blank in both purchase agreements, and Thor retains the right to remove any assumed contract before closing; because the debtors contract through FlowX rather than directly with TNMP, the record does not yet establish which supply, scheduling, or interconnection agreements would transfer with the assets.
 
The Assigned Contracts Schedule, with proposed cure amounts, is due August 21, 2026
 — a week after the bidding-procedures hearing, meaning the question of what power rights actually transfer will not be resolved before Judge O'Hagan rules on the sale framework. For the 11,700 wallet holders carrying $163,723,500 in unsecured IOU claims, 
the prepetition marketing process produced three other indications of interest, leaving room for competition without establishing that another qualified offer will emerge; the amount available to wallet creditors will then depend on estate-specific claims, valid liens against net proceeds, transfer taxes, professional fees, other administrative costs, and the treatment of Poolin's intercompany claim.
 The bidding-procedures and sale hearing before Judge O'Hagan, August 14 at 11 a.m. ET, is the next concrete milestone on which the entire downstream September calendar turns.

items.body_md:
On August 8 and 9, no new docket entries appeared in Case No. 26-90737, and no substantive press coverage landed over the weekend. The case is in the interval between the August 7 lift-stay filing at Dkt. 146 and the August 24 second-day hearing.

The lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146 remains the live open item. The movant, asset at stake, and specific relief sought remain unconfirmed from a primary-source pull; the affidavits at Dkts. 156 and 157, filed the same day, are the most likely evidentiary support, but that interpretation is unverified until the documents are pulled from PACER. What is established from the docket is that service was completed per the BNC certificate at Dkt. 158. Under the standard 14-day contested-matter timeline in the Southern District of Texas, a response deadline of approximately August 21 falls three days before the August 24 second-day hearing — positioning Dkt. 146 as a live candidate for that docket, either as a contested matter or by agreed resolution before the hearing date. The Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors, constituted August 6 (Dkt. 137), will also make its first formal appearance at that hearing; its posture on the lift-stay motion — and on any interim-to-final conversion of first-day orders — is unknown until it files or speaks at the podium.

The next concrete milestone is the second-day hearing on August 24, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. CT before Judge Lopez. The schedules of assets and liabilities and statements of financial affairs remain due September 23, 2026.
